metadata.name: bayla_ladder
metadata.description: Lock-ladder staking with a flat 25% early exit — the Solana port of LighthouseLadder.sol

instructions.name: cancel_cap_raise
docs: AUDIT L-7. `propose_cap_raise` requires `new_cap > deposit_cap`, so a pending
proposal could be shrunk to +1 but never returned to zero — and
`execute_cap_raise` is permissionless with no staleness check, so a proposal made
a year ago stays executable on demand. This is the missing half: the authority
can abandon its own proposal. Adds no Pool fields, so every pinned size holds.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Claim rewards without closing anything. Pays what the reward vault can cover;
the rest stays owed (I-2).

instructions.name: claim_carried
docs: Pay out rewards a position carried into `UserStats` when it left through the
emergency hatch. Same I-2 rule: pays what the vault holds, defers the rest.

instructions.name: declare_degraded
docs: ONE-WAY. After this, the emergency hatch charges no penalty while locked.

instructions.name: early_exit
docs: Leave BEFORE the lock ends: principal minus 25%, rewards paid. The penalty
stays in the pool as reward budget.

instructions.name: emergency_withdraw
docs: THE LAST RESORT. Principal only, at ANY time — including while locked (paying
the 25% unless the pool is degraded) and including when the reward vault is
empty, closed, or wedged. This instruction declares NO reward vault (I-12).
AUDIT C3: it still checkpoints, because a checkpoint is pure accounting and
cannot fail on a vault — and skipping it would shrink the accumulator's divisor
without banking the window, repricing every other staker retroactively. The
caller's own accrual is preserved in `UserStats.rewards_carried`, claimable
later via `claim_carried`, rather than deleted with the position.

instructions.name: execute_cap_raise
docs: Permissionless once the timelock has elapsed.

instructions.name: initialize_pool
docs: Create a pool for `mint`. Deployer-gated (see [`deployer`]). Runs the mint gate
once, pins the token program to the mint's actual owner, and creates both vaults.

instructions.name: notify_reward
docs: Open a 90-day window. Owner decision 2026-09-06: reload every 90 days, distribute
per second.
TWO SOURCES, deliberately separated (AUDIT H-1):
`amount`      fresh tokens transferred in by the authority in THIS instruction.
Counted into `reward_funded_cumulative`, which is why the transfer
lives here rather than being inferred from a balance.
`from_budget` tokens ALREADY in the reward vault and not yet pledged — retained
early-exit penalties, swept emergency-hatch penalties, the
un-emitted tail of a lapsed window, a stranger's donation.
Before the split, the rate was a pure function of `amount`, so every token in the
second category was permanently unspendable: lifetime emission could not exceed
the sum of the `amount`s, and there is no `recover_tokens` and no `close_pool`.
The pool promised leavers' penalties to whoever stayed (`exit_with_penalty`) and
could not deliver them. `sweep_orphaned_penalty` moved tokens into a vault they
could never leave.
Solvency is unchanged and is still what bounds this: the resulting rate is checked
against `fundable()`, the real vault balance minus everything already owed. Naming
`from_budget` cannot conjure a token — it can only point the schedule at one that
is physically present and unpledged.

instructions.name: propose_cap_raise
docs: I-13. Raise-only. Takes effect after `CAP_TIMELOCK_SECS` via `execute_cap_raise`.

instructions.name: stake
docs: Open a position. Every stake is its OWN position: no top-up, so no boost
blending and no way to buy a high multiplier for a short commitment.

accounts.name: user_stats
docs: Declared BEFORE `position`: its `next_nonce` seeds the position, and Anchor
evaluates constraints in declaration order.

instructions.name: sweep_orphaned_penalty
docs: Permissionless. Carries penalties the emergency hatch left in the stake vault
across to the reward vault. Fixed destination — no discretion, nothing to steer.

instructions.name: withdraw_matured
docs: Close a MATURED position: principal in full, rewards paid.

errors.name: Overflow
errors.msg: Arithmetic overflow

errors.name: ZeroAmount
errors.msg: Amount resolves to zero

errors.name: LockTooShort
errors.msg: Lock is shorter than the seven-day floor

errors.name: LockTooLong
errors.msg: Lock is longer than the four-year ceiling

errors.name: BelowMinStake
errors.msg: Stake is below the pool minimum — measured on what arrived, not what was sent

errors.name: TooManyPositions
errors.msg: This wallet already holds the maximum number of open positions on this pool

errors.name: DepositCapExceeded
errors.msg: Deposit would exceed the pool's cap

errors.name: StillLocked
errors.msg: Position is still locked — use early_exit or emergency_withdraw (25% penalty)

errors.name: UseWithdrawMatured
errors.msg: Position has matured — use withdraw_matured; it must not eat a penalty by accident

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.msg: Only the configured authority may do this

errors.name: NotDeployAuthority
errors.msg: Program not initialized by the designated deployer

errors.name: MintHasFreezeAuthority
errors.msg: Mint carries a freeze authority — it could freeze the vault and trap every staker's principal

errors.name: UnsupportedMintExtension
errors.msg: Mint carries an extension this pool does not accept (transfer fee, hook, permanent delegate, ...)

errors.name: WrongTokenProgram
errors.msg: Token program does not match the mint's owner

errors.name: RewardTooHigh
errors.msg: Reward rate exceeds what the vault can fund after reserving what is already owed

errors.name: CapCanOnlyRaise
errors.msg: The deposit cap can only be raised, never lowered

errors.name: TimelockNotElapsed
errors.msg: The timelock on this change has not elapsed

errors.name: NoPendingChange
errors.msg: There is no pending change to execute

errors.name: InvalidParameter
errors.msg: Configured value is outside its permitted range

errors.name: AlreadyDegraded
errors.msg: Pool is already degraded — the flag is one-way

errors.name: EmissionExceedsFunding
errors.msg: Emission exceeds funding plus collected penalties — refusing to pay rewards out of principal

errors.name: PrincipalInvariant
errors.msg: Stake vault holds less than tracked principal — refusing to proceed

errors.name: WeightInvariant
errors.msg: Position weight exceeds pool total — ledger is desynchronised

errors.name: NothingToSweep
errors.msg: Nothing to sweep

errors.name: RewardRateTooSmall
errors.msg: Reward amount is too small to express as a per-second rate over the window — it would emit nothing

errors.name: MintHasMintAuthority
errors.msg: Mint carries a live mint authority — it could conjure the asset this pool prices

errors.name: PoolDegraded
errors.msg: This pool has been declared degraded — it accepts no new stakes; existing positions exit penalty-free

errors.name: WalletCapExceeded
errors.msg: This wallet already holds its maximum share of the pool

types.name: AuthorityProposed
docs: AUDIT L-11. The admin surface emitted nothing typed. Anchor injects
`msg!("Instruction: <Name>")` into every handler so nothing was silent, but the log
carries the NAME and not the VALUES — an indexer had to make a second
`getTransaction` hop to learn what changed. `sweep_orphaned_penalty` was also the
only token-moving instruction with no `emit!` at all. IDL-additive; no pinned size
moves, because events are not accounts.

fields.name: executable_at
docs: When `execute_cap_raise` becomes callable.

fields.name: amount
docs: Moved stake vault -> reward vault, and now schedulable via `notify_reward`'s
`from_budget` (audit H-1). Before that fix this event would have described a
no-op.

types.name: Pool
docs: One pool per (mint, nonce). PDA at [`POOL_SEED`, mint, nonce].
Every cumulative quantity is u128 — see `math.rs` for the Streamflow lesson.
`total_principal` is a TRACKED SCALAR and authoritative: it is never derived from
the vault balance, because any stranger can transfer into the vault, so only
`vault >= total_principal` is a safe statement (invariant I-1).

fields.name: token_program
docs: Pinned at init to whatever program actually owns the mint. Every transfer is
checked against it.

fields.name: authority
docs: Admin. Two-step transfer (`propose_authority` / `accept_authority`).

fields.name: min_stake
docs: Smallest stake this pool admits, in raw base units, measured on what ARRIVED.
`>= math::HARD_MIN_STAKE_RAW`; it derives the I-11 divisor floor.

fields.name: deposit_cap
docs: Invariant I-13. Raise-only, on a 48 h timelock. The one lever that genuinely
buys back safety for a program with no deployment record: ship it low and
ratchet as the program ages.

fields.name: max_wallet_principal
docs: AUDIT M-4. The pool-wide cap alone let ONE wallet occupy a whole low-cap pool
and refuse every other depositor indefinitely — `MAX_POSITIONS` bounds client
enumeration, not capital, and a single position may be the entire cap. There is
no forced maturity, decay or kick, so the position simply sits there.
Deliberately NOT a sentinel: there is no "0 means unlimited". A pool that wants
no per-wallet limit sets this equal to `deposit_cap`, which is explicit and
cannot be reached by forgetting to configure it. Carved from `_reserved`, so
`8 + Pool::INIT_SPACE` stays 508.

fields.name: total_principal
docs: REAL principal, exactly as Synthetix means `_totalSupply`. Authoritative.

fields.name: total_weighted
docs: Sum of every open position's weight. The accumulator's divisor.

fields.name: reward_rate
docs: Synthetix state, unchanged in meaning.

fields.name: rewards_emitted
docs: AUDIT C2 (LighthouseLadder.sol): total the accumulator has ever emitted, and
the part already transferred out. Their difference is the outstanding
liability, reserved before any new period may be funded (I-3).

fields.name: reward_funded_cumulative
docs: TELEMETRY, not an enforced bound (audit L-3 — both are write-only on-chain,
and the docstrings that claimed otherwise were wrong). The enforced solvency
check is in `notify_reward`: outstanding liability must be physically present
in the reward vault.
`reward_funded_cumulative` counts only tokens moved IN by `notify_reward`, so
a stranger's direct transfer is usable budget but is not counted here.
`penalty_collected_cumulative` counts retained early-exit penalties and swept
emergency-hatch penalties. Since H-1, both categories are genuinely
schedulable via `notify_reward`'s `from_budget`, so the split between them is
now meaningful rather than decorative: it is how an operator answers "how much
of what this pool paid came from leavers rather than from me".

fields.name: orphaned_penalty
docs: A penalty charged by `emergency_withdraw`, which declares NO reward vault
(I-12), is left in the stake vault and tracked here until the permissionless
`sweep_orphaned_penalty` moves it to the reward vault. It is never principal:
`total_principal` already excludes it.

fields.name: degraded
docs: ONE-WAY. When set, `emergency_withdraw` charges no penalty while locked. This
is the answer to "what if the operator is the failure": a flag that can only
ever move in the direction that frees stakers gives a stolen key nothing it
wants. Its cost is honest — it stops future penalty inflow.

fields.name: rpw_residue
docs: Truncation remainders (audit M-2 / L-4). Carved OUT of `_reserved` rather than
appended, so `8 + Pool::INIT_SPACE` stays at its pinned 508 and no already-
deployed pool would need migrating. `rpw_residue` carries
`num % total_weighted` from the accumulator step; `emitted_residue` carries
`num % PRECISION` from the pool-side bank. Both are dropped, never banked,
across an I-11-burned or empty-pool interval.

types.name: Position
docs: One position. PDA at [`POSITION_SEED`, pool, owner, nonce_le]. Every stake is its
OWN position — there is no top-up, so there is no boost blending and no way to buy
a high multiplier for a short commitment.
A closed position is DELETED (`close = owner`), never zeroed and left behind.
All three criticals in the EVM design review began with a record that outlived
its close (invariant I-7).

fields.name: amount
docs: Principal, in raw base units — what ARRIVED.

fields.name: weight
docs: `amount x boost / BPS`, frozen at stake time.

fields.name: reward_per_weight_paid
docs: Synthetix `userRewardPerTokenPaid`.

fields.name: rewards_owed
docs: Synthetix `rewards[]` — accrued and not yet paid. Deferred, never forfeited,
when the vault is short (I-2).

fields.name: _reserved
docs: AUDIT L-8, and it is FREE NOW AND IMPOSSIBLE LATER. `Pool` reserved padding and
these two did not. An upgrade that grows this struct fails Borsh (3003) on every
pre-existing account across all four exit paths, and `stake` fails one step
earlier on `ConstraintSpace` (2019). Recoverable by redeploying the prior
binary — but only because nothing is live yet.
Padding only helps ADDITIVE growth. Reordering or widening an existing field
still breaks every account, reserve or no reserve.

fields.name: amount
docs: Fresh tokens transferred in by this call.

fields.name: from_budget
docs: Tokens already in the vault that this call scheduled (AUDIT H-1). An indexer
must add the two to get what the window will actually pay.

fields.name: deferred
docs: What is STILL owed after this payment — non-zero means the vault was short and
the balance is deferred, not lost.

types.name: UserStats
docs: Per-(pool, wallet) bookkeeping. PDA at [`USER_SEED`, pool, owner].
The nonce is PROGRAM-ASSIGNED and monotone, so a client can never collide with
itself, and no `Vec<Pubkey>` of position ids lives on-chain — the client
enumerates with `getProgramAccounts` + memcmp on `owner`, exactly as
`bungalowStaking.ts` already does against Streamflow.

fields.name: rewards_carried
docs: Rewards a position was owed when it closed through a path that could not (or
did not fully) pay them — the emergency hatch, which has no reward vault, or an
exit against a short vault. AUDIT C3 in the Solidity keeps these in a per-
account `rewards[]` that survives the position; this is that ledger. Paid by
`claim_carried` under the same I-2 rule: what the vault holds now, the rest
deferred. Deferred, never forfeited.

fields.name: principal
docs: This wallet's live principal in this pool, against `Pool::max_wallet_principal`
(audit M-4). MUST be decremented on every close — `debit_closed` does it — or a
wallet self-locks out of the pool after its first exit, which would turn a
fairness guard into a denial of service against honest users.

fields.name: _reserved
docs: See `Position::_reserved` — same reasoning, smaller struct (audit L-8).

fields.name: amount
docs: What the staker RECEIVED.

fields.name: penalty
docs: What the pool kept. Zero on a matured withdrawal.

fields.name: emergency
docs: true = the reward-vault-free hatch; false = a normal exit.
